findings.evidenceJa: まずい、きっと桜が帰ってきたんだ！
findings.governingReading: Shirou realizes the time and guesses Sakura has returned.
findings.explanation: The English inserts a sudden standing action absent from the active Japanese witness.

findings.evidenceJa: 先輩……？　あの、お夕飯の支度なんですけど……
findings.governingReading: Sakura hesitantly raises the matter of preparing dinner.
findings.explanation: The English restores a commented-out worried gaze, fixing Sakura’s internal reaction more explicitly than the active scene does.

findings.highlight: There is a flashy, fiery sound coming from the kitchen
findings.evidenceJa: 台所ではジャージャーと派手な音がしている
findings.governingReading: Loud, showy sizzling and clattering comes from the kitchen.
findings.explanation: “Fiery sound” misreads an onomatopoeic cooking noise and produces unnatural English.

findings.highlight: So there’s no point in staying here. There’s Saber to think about, so I should go back to my room until dinner is prepared.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの事もあるし、できるまで部屋に戻っていよう
findings.governingReading: With Saber also on his mind, Shirou decides to return to his room until dinner is ready.
findings.explanation: The English inserts an unsupported claim that remaining there is pointless.

findings.highlight: didn’t I have trouble talking to Saber?
findings.evidenceJa: 自分はセイバーが苦手ではなかったのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou reminds himself that he was uncomfortable with or poor at dealing with Saber.
findings.explanation: The English narrows his broader interpersonal discomfort to conversational difficulty.

findings.highlight: I say that and just stare at the clock.
findings.evidenceJa: ぼんやりと口にして、ただ時計の針だけを眺めた
findings.governingReading: Shirou says it absently and does nothing but watch the clock hands.
findings.explanation: The English omits his absent, unfocused delivery, flattening the mood that leads into thoughts of Saber’s isolation.

findings.evidenceJa: 無性に腹が立ってきた
findings.governingReading: The image of Saber eating alone makes Shirou unaccountably angry.
findings.explanation: “Annoying me” weakens a sudden surge of anger and can misassign it to Saber rather than the imagined isolation.

findings.highlight: a plate full of steamed meat dumplings
findings.evidenceJa: 何を考えているのか皿一杯のシューマイ軍団
findings.governingReading: One platter holds an absurd full army of shumai.
findings.explanation: The English gives the food generically and drops the comic “army” image and narrator’s incredulous aside.

findings.highlight: some stir-fry of an elegant looking meat I’ve never seen before with vegetables
findings.evidenceJa: なんか見たこともないような上品そうな肉と野菜の炒めもの
findings.governingReading: Another platter holds an elegant-looking meat-and-vegetable stir-fry unlike anything Shirou has seen.
findings.explanation: The English makes the meat itself unknown and elegant-looking, misattaching the description of the unfamiliar dish.

findings.highlight: There are salads on the side plates, and various follow-ups are ready.
findings.evidenceJa: 口休めのサラダ等が用意されており、細かいフォローも行き届いている
findings.governingReading: Small plates include salads as palate cleansers, showing attention to supporting details.
findings.explanation: “Various follow-ups” copies the Japanese abstraction into opaque English and loses the culinary function.

findings.highlight: when I told that her no one at our house cooks Chinese
findings.evidenceJa: けど中華料理は誰も作らないって言ったら
findings.governingReading: Sakura says that when she told Rin nobody in the household cooked Chinese food, Rin volunteered to make it.
findings.explanation: The English word order is grammatically malformed.

findings.highlight: Why does she have to live her life poking at holes?
findings.evidenceJa: なんでそう隙間を突くような人生しか送れないのかアイツは
findings.governingReading: Shirou jokes that Rin can only live by finding and exploiting every open niche.
findings.explanation: The literal “poking at holes” is non-English and loses the competitive opportunism of the joke.

findings.highlight: Saying this coldly, Tohsaka sits down as well.
findings.evidenceJa: そっけなく言って、遠坂も食卓についた
findings.governingReading: Rin delivers the line curtly and sits at the table.
findings.explanation: “Coldly” overstates emotional hostility in a playful household exchange.

findings.highlight: Everyone bows and eats the food.
findings.evidenceJa: 全員がいただきます、とお辞儀をして料理を口にした
findings.governingReading: Everyone bows, says itadakimasu, and begins eating.
findings.explanation: The English omits the shared spoken mealtime greeting that marks the four diners acting together.

findings.highlight: I am pleased to receive an honest response like that.
findings.evidenceJa: 先生のように素直に感想を言ってもらえると、わたしも嬉しいです
findings.governingReading: Rin says she is pleased when someone gives an honest reaction the way their teacher does.
findings.explanation: The English omits the explicit comparison to Fuji-nee, weakening Rin’s response to her particular personality.

findings.highlight: I’m not good with hot food
findings.evidenceJa: 辛いのって苦手なんですけど
findings.governingReading: Sakura says she is not good with spicy food.
findings.explanation: The English changes spiciness into temperature.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka Rin looks at me with an expression of triumph.
findings.evidenceJa: 性根の曲がった遠坂凛
findings.governingReading: After smiling at Sakura, the “crooked-natured” Rin turns a triumphant look on Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English omits Shirou’s comic judgment of Rin’s character, leaving only the surface expression.

findings.highlight: Today’s lesson is, always hide your potential.
findings.evidenceJa: 今日の教訓は、手の内は常に隠しておく、でしたー
findings.governingReading: Rin turns the cooking contest into a mock tactical lesson: always keep what is in your hand, your capabilities or cards, concealed.
findings.explanation: Repeating “potential” flattens the 手の内 metaphor and weakens the joke connecting cooking rivalry to tactical secrecy.
